newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end up on late buying of blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end up on late buying of blue-chips.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended higher on late buying of top blue-chips, but analysts showed some disappointment with the market's thin volume.
The Bovespa Index .BVSP of the 49 most traded stocks rose 1.04 percent, closing at 67,356 points. Turnover was 224.50 million reais ($217.4 million).
Traders said a short-covering movement late in the session amid speculation ahead of mid-December's options and futures settlement also helped to boost the index.
Benchmark Telebras rose 1.66 percent to close at 79.50 reais.
State power utility Eletrobras preferred rose 1.47 percent to 344 reais, while state oil firm Petrobras gained 1.03 percent to 99.50 reais.
Preferred shares of Sao Paulo state bank Banespa also continued rising on Monday and jumped 8.51 percent to 6.50 reais.
Banespa's preferred stock has surged 35.4 percent since trade in the bank resumed last Friday after a three-day suspension.

Traders said the stock price had been reflecting optimism about the future of the bank after Sao Paulo state accepted to hand it over to the federal government in a move seen by analysts as a step leading to privatization.
Analysts also said stocks could continue posting moderate gains on Tuesday, but noted that investor mood could change if November export figures, due out tomorrow, fail to cheer the market.
In October, Brazil posted a $1.3 billion trade deficit on exports of $4.188 billion and imports of $5.496 billion.
For November, the market has been speculating Brazil will post a trade deficit between $700 million and $1.0 billion.
